subject: Recap + MAP: technical evaluation criteria and milestones for Atlas Health
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dawson <claire@atlashealth.ai>, Atlas Health EngOps <engops@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Recap: Technical MAP & next steps — Atlas Health evaluation

Claire / team — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and a first-pass MAP draft for the technical evaluation milestone we discussed. I've attached a 1-page MAP draft (atlas-map-draft-v1.pdf) — please consider this the working version we can iterate on.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary use case: patient triage / pre-visit summarization (short prompts, ~40–150 tokens output).
- Success emphasis: response quality (Q/A accuracy), low tail latency for interactive flow, predictable per-token cost for scale.
- Internal evaluator: Raj (Eng) will lead the bench run & provide the sample dataset.

Proposed MAP items (high level):
1) Technical evaluation plan (this thread) — deliverable: benchmark report + recommended model/quant profile
   - Responsible: Redwood (Vanessa, Sergio) + Atlas Eng (Raj)
   - Target completion: 2026-03-12 (4 weeks)
2) Security & compliance checklist — Atlas to confirm required logs/data handling (parallel)
3) Pilot integration and POC (2–3 weeks after bench pass)

Immediate asks / dependencies from Atlas:
- Provide a representative sample set (250–500 anonymized prompts + expected outputs) by 2026-02-18.
- Grant temporary test access to a staging endpoint or share an S3 bucket with artifacts.
- Confirm target SLOs (latency and cost) or approve the targets below.

Draft technical evaluation (short version) — please review and flag changes: 
- Benchmark sample: 250 prompts across 4 categories (triage, summary, follow-up Qs, policy checks).
- Quality targets: automated QA accuracy >= 88% (on agreed scoring script), hallucination rate < 5% on sample set.
- Latency targets (interactive flows, median prompt length ~80 tokens): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms (single-request, cold cache), sustained throughput target 40 RPS with <10% tail degradation.
- Cost target: operational inference cost <= $25 per 1M output tokens (striped to avoid counting internal caching).
- Model shortlist: Llama-3-13B (4-bit quant), Mistral-Instruct-7B (8-bit), Falcon-40B-instruct (8-bit), OpenAssistant-6B (quantized). Redwood will include quantized variants tuned for latency/cost tradeoffs.

Next steps I propose:
- Claire / Raj: confirm you can share the 250-sample set by 02/18 and confirm that Raj should receive runner access.
- Atlas: confirm whether the latency targets above are acceptable or propose adjustments by 02/16.
- Redwood: we'll produce a bench plan (microbench + application-level eval) and a benchmark-config.yaml for your review by 02/14.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: atlas-map-draft-v1.pdf (1 page MAP draft)

From: Claire Dawson <claire@atlashealth.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T17:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Technical MAP & next steps — Atlas Health evaluation

Thanks Vanessa — this looks good and aligns with our internal expectations. Quick notes: 
- Raj will own the bench runs and I copied EngOps to coordinate infra. He can take the dataset and run the Redwood configs in our staging.
- Can we tighten the p95 latency goal to 200ms? Our product team wants sub-200ms feel for users. If that's not realistic for the larger models, call it out.
- Target close: we were hoping to aim for an agreement by end of March (2026-03-31) if the bench and pilot look good.

I'll ask Raj to share the sample set by 2026-02-18. Attaching our format spec (atlas-reqs.csv).

— Claire
Claire Dawson
Head of Product — Atlas Health
claire@atlashealth.ai

Attachment: atlas-reqs.csv

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dawson <claire@atlashealth.ai>, Raj Patel <raj@atlashealth.ai>, Atlas Health EngOps <engops@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-13T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Updated MAP: Technical eval plan + benchmarks (inc. p95 goal)

Claire / Raj — thanks for the quick reply and for pushing the sample set timeline. We can aim to meet a stricter p95 target; I'll surface tradeoffs below and include them in the bench plan we send tomorrow. Updated items: 

1) Adjusted latency targets (interactive prompts, ~80 token outputs):
   - p50 < 70ms
   - p95 < 200ms (target) — note: this is plausible for lighter models or aggressive quantization on gen-class GPUs; for larger models (Falcon-40B) expect p95 to be higher unless using larger instance sizes or batching strategies.
2) Bench plan (deliverables):
   - Microbench: single-request latency distribution (cold vs warmed cache) across 4 model candidates; per-instance throughput curves.
   - Application-level eval: run 250-sample set through each model variant, compute QA accuracy, hallucination metric, and a perplexity/likelihood delta against Atlas gold answers.
   - Cost estimate: simulate 1M output tokens at observed throughput to provide per-1M token cost and 95% CI.
3) Success criteria (pass/fail gate for pilot):
   - QA accuracy >= 88% AND hallucination rate < 5%
   - p95 <= 200ms OR documented ops mitigations (edge caching, routing to smaller model for interactive flows) that keep UX sub-200ms 90% of the time.
   - Estimated cost within agreed target (<= $25 / 1M tokens).
4) Model shortlist/variants we will test:
   - Llama-3-13B (4-bit quant) — primary candidate for best latency/cost balance
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (8-bit) — strong quality / small footprint
   - Falcon-40B-instruct (8-bit) — quality upper bound, higher infra cost
   - OpenAssistant-6B (quant) — ultra-low-cost baseline

Dependencies & schedule:
- Atlas provides dataset and temporary staging endpoint (or S3 access) by 02/18.
- Redwood delivers benchmark-config.yaml + orchestration plan by 02/14.
- Bench runs scheduled 02/19–02/24 (flexible, need ~4–6h of window with stable infra).
- Bench report + recommendation by 03/03.

If OK, we'll treat the March 31 target close as the commercial milestone and work backwards from the bench report -> pilot -> contract review. Sergio & Aditya — tagging you for any technical caveats on infra sizing or recommended instance classes.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-13T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: bench config notes for Atlas (quick)

Vanessa / Aditya — quick technical notes to seed the config we'll attach to the MAP doc: 
- Run microbench on g5.2xlarge-equivalent and g5.12xlarge-equivalent to show scaling curves.
- Test batch sizes 1, 4, 8 for each quant profile; measure p50/p95 and memory footprint.
- Include caching experiments (prefix cache for repeated prefixes in triage flows) — expect 20–35% token cost reduction.
- Provide model-variant tags in benchmark output so we can recommend a single config for pilot (e.g., llama3-13b-q4a, mistral-instruct-7b-q8, falcon-40b-q8).

I'll attach the initial YAML (redwood-benchmark-config.yaml) and a short CSV template for results. We should keep the report binary-free and include links to graphs in Drive.

— Sergio
Director, Applied ML — Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-benchmark-config.yaml
